market_name: Will OpenAI not IPO by December 31, 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check for any OpenAI IPO/funding headlines or S-1 chatter; confirm whether the Polymarket probability shift coincides with a news catalyst rather than thin-market noise.
time_plan.1h: Compare MSFT intraday move to Nasdaq/QQQ and AI peers to isolate any OpenAI-specific component vs broad tech beta.
time_plan.2h: Re-check whether volume/price in MSFT deviates from sector; if no divergence, treat signal as noise.
time_plan.6h: Scan newswires for confirmation of IPO timeline changes or banker mandates; reassess whether the prediction-market move was informed.
time_plan.12h: Mark final MSFT return vs QQQ; log whether any predictive edge existed. Expect none given the structural nature of the question.

predictions.reasoning: Microsoft is OpenAI's largest external investor and commercial partner, so any shift in expectations about an OpenAI IPO (valuation, timing, monetization) has the cleanest liquid public-market proxy in MSFT. However, an IPO-timing question is a slow-moving structural corporate-finance event, not a market-moving surprise on a 12h horizon. Even a sharp move in the implied probability of 'No IPO by 2026' carries ambiguous sign for MSFT: an earlier IPO could crystallize/mark up MSFT's stake value (bullish) but also dilute or reprice the partnership; a delayed IPO signals nothing acutely negative. The link to a same-day price move is tenuous.

evidence_used: Market question concerns OpenAI IPO timing/market cap by Dec 31 2026
OpenAI is private; the only liquid public proxies are large investors/partners, chiefly Microsoft
No specific catalyst or dated event embedded in the question — it is a long-horizon structural probability
uncertainty_notes: A 12h window is far too short for a 2026 IPO-timing question to produce a reliable asset move
Direction of MSFT reaction to IPO timing news is genuinely ambiguous (mark-up vs dilution/repricing)
Polymarket odds on this question are likely thin and noisy, easily moved without new information
Miscategorized as 'elections' topic suggests weak/unreliable metadata

llm_justification.summary: This market asks whether OpenAI will delay its IPO past end-2026 — a slow structural corporate-finance question with no acute catalyst. The only liquid public proxy is Microsoft as OpenAI's largest investor/partner. Even a sharp probability move would map only weakly and with ambiguous sign onto MSFT over a 12h window, well below the 700bp tradability threshold. We flag this as an essentially untradable, low-confidence mapping.
key_assumptions: Microsoft remains the dominant liquid proxy for OpenAI valuation expectations
No concurrent, unrelated MSFT catalyst dominates the tape
Prediction-market move reflects at most modest, non-market-moving information
failure_modes: The probability move is pure thin-market noise with zero information content
IPO timing is already broadly public/priced, so no asset reaction occurs
MSFT is a weak proxy — its market cap dwarfs any plausible OpenAI stake revaluation, diluting the signal
Sign is wrong: delayed IPO could be read as bullish (retention) or bearish (monetization concerns) inconsistently
12h horizon captures none of the eventual repricing, which would occur only on an actual filing
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
